issues.description: The return type of messageOnMilk() is inconsistent across the problem statement UML, the textual description, the template usage, and the solution. The UML for the Milkable interface (problem statement) declares messageOnMilk():boolean and the textual instructions state it should return true/false, while the class-level UML entries for Seal and Goat and the solution code define messageOnMilk() as returning String. The template Main also prints the return value (System.out.println(m.messageOnMilk())), which works with either type but is ambiguous given the conflicting specification. This mismatch will confuse students about whether to implement messageOnMilk() to return a boolean or a String and blocks a straightforward implementation aligned with the specification.
issues.suggestedFix: Decide on a single return type for messageOnMilk() across the exercise and make all artifacts consistent. Either: (A) specify in the problem statement and UML that Milkable.messageOnMilk() returns String (and update the textual instruction to show example strings like "Goat [name] is milked"), or (B) change the solution and template usage to use boolean returns (and update Seal/Goat implementations and any places that print the result). Prefer updating the problem statement/UML to String to match the solution and the intended printable messages.

issues.description: The Milkable.messageOnMilk concept is inconsistent across artifacts: the problem statement (UML and explicit text) defines messageOnMilk() as returning a boolean (and even states it should return true/false), while other parts of the problem UML list Seal.messageOnMilk() as returning a String. The provided solution implements Milkable.messageOnMilk() and the concrete implementations (Goat, Seal) to return String messages (e.g., "Goat [name] is milked"). This mismatch (boolean vs. String) creates confusion about the expected API and behavior students should implement.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Milkable.messageOnMilk() contract consistent across all artifacts. Either: (A) Update the problem statement UML and text to declare messageOnMilk():String and describe that it should return a descriptive message (e.g., "Goat [name] is milked"), matching the solution; or (B) change the solution and implementations (Milkable, Goat, Seal) to return boolean and adjust the concrete classes and example outputs accordingly. Align all references (UML diagrams, textual requirements, template comments) to the chosen signature so students can map requirements to implementation unambiguously.
